cards.text: John is writing to believers he calls beloved, and he just told them God has given them His Spirit. Now he's got a warning: don't believe every spirit. Baker, that's me with every text that says I won a FREE cruise.

cards.question: John tells his beloved readers not to believe every spirit. What should they do instead?

answers.text: Test them to see if they're from God
Stay far away from every spirit
Trust the one that sounds the kindest

cards.question: Why do John's readers need to test the spirits? Because many false ___ have gone out into the world.

cards.text: Test before you trust? Friend, I RESPECT that. I test every batch before it goes in a box. One bite. Okay, four bites. Quality control.
So how do you test a spirit? John says it all comes down to what it says about Jesus.

cards.question: John gives the test: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the ___ is from God.
John says a spirit that does not confess Jesus can still be from God.

cards.text: John even gives that spirit a name. It's the spirit of the antichrist, and his readers had already heard it was coming.

cards.question: John's readers had heard the spirit of the antichrist was coming. Where does John say it is?

answers.text: Already in the world right now

cards.text: False prophets out there AND that spirit already here? Friend, I'd be diving back under the takeout menus in my old junk drawer. But John's got good news for his readers.

cards.question: John calls his readers little children and tells them they're from God and have overcome. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The One in them is greater than the one in the world
They outnumber the false prophets in the world
They studied harder than the false prophets did

cards.text: Then John turns back to the false prophets. He says they are of the world.

cards.question: Since these false prophets are of the world, how do they speak?
John says the world refuses to listen to the false prophets.

cards.text: Of COURSE the world listens. That's like asking your own group chat if your idea is good. Then John says, "We are from God."

cards.question: John says some people listen to "us" and some don't. Who does he say listens?
John says who listens and who doesn't is how we know the Spirit of ___ and the spirit of ___.

findings.problem: John appears for the first time with no simple description of who he is. The baker isn't told he's one of Jesus' disciples or an apostle.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card states as fact that John is writing the letter. 1 John never names its author, so there's no verse to cite for this. The docs allow outside facts like who wrote a letter only "with their reference."
findings.question: For a letter whose author the text doesn't name, like 1 John, should Papa Dorin name John as the writer (and how should that be cited), or describe the writer without a name?

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats the 'test the spirits' idea already covered on cards 1 to 3 just to carry a joke. It is a recap card citing 1 John 4:1 without moving the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank quotes the line of 4:2 and blanks its last word ('flesh'). Nothing on earlier cards lets the baker reason out 'flesh' over 'clouds' or 'fire', so it tests wording the baker hasn't seen. It should ask about the meaning of the test instead.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Where does John say it is?' The right answer gives a place ('in the world'), but both wrong answers are times ('Waiting until the very end', 'Still many years away'). The answers aren't the same kind of thing, and the wrong answers don't fit a where question.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It echoes the familiar wording of the verse and capitalizes 'One' against a lowercase 'one', which signals God. It is also noticeably longer than the wrong answers, while 'They studied harder than the false prophets did' sounds modern and casual next to it.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Whoever lives nearby' doesn't match the tone of the other answers. It reads as throwaway next to 'Whoever knows God' and 'Whoever is from the world', so it's easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
